key_insight: The paper introduces action priors that help robot policies start with a better sense of motion, rather than learning physical behavior from scratch. This makes cross-embodiment manipulation easier by separating “how to move” from “what to perceive.”
problem_solved: Existing VLA models reuse strong vision-language knowledge but often lack an explicit motion prior in the action module. This forces the policy to learn temporal action dynamics and cross-modal alignment at the same time, which is especially difficult across different robot embodiments.
method: Learn action priors to initialize or guide the robot action module with motion knowledge before full policy training.
Design the policy to better transfer manipulation behavior across different robot bodies/embodiments.
Reduce the burden on end-to-end training by decoupling motion learning from vision-language grounding.
impact: For practitioners, this can improve sample efficiency, training stability, and transferability in robot manipulation systems. It is especially relevant for building robots that generalize across platforms without retraining everything from scratch.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing VLM backbone + action module + learned action prior.

An icon-based flow chart separating perception, motion prior learning, and policy execution.
paper_title: Learning Action Priors for Cross-embodiment Robot Manipulation
paper_authors: Dong Jing, Tianqi Zhang, Jiaqi Liu, Jinman Zhao, Zelong Sun
